One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

type.description: What kind of feedback this is.

title.description: Short, specific one-line summary of the issue.

details.description: Labeled bullets, in order: **What happened:** (observed vs. expected, exact error text if short); **What the user said:** (quoted, or "User didn't comment; observed by the model."); **Repro:** (minimal steps); **Evidence:** (request IDs, timestamps, paths, versions; omit if none); optionally a final **Cause:** only if verified in-session. One to three lines per bullet. No narrative paragraphs, no speculation, no secrets.

area.description: Optional short tag naming the part of Claude Code this is about (e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing"). Leave blank if unclear.

failure_mode.description: When the report is about MODEL BEHAVIOR (not a product bug), the closest failure mode, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value. Omit only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.

task_category.description: What kind of task the session was doing when the issue occurred, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: WebFetch
tools.description:
Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead. claude.ai artifact links (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}) are published artifacts: read them with the Artifact tool (action "read"), not WebFetch or curl.
- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

url.description: The URL to fetch content from

prompt.description: The prompt to run on the fetched content

offset.description: Character position in the page text to start reading from. Use it to read on through a page too long for one call, with the value the previous result gave.

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to write (must be absolute, not relative)

content.description: The content to write to the file

tools.name: mcp__plugin_design_notion__notion-create-pages
tools.description:
Creates one or more Notion pages with the specified properties and content.

## Core rules

**IMPORTANT**: Before writing page content, read the MCP resource `notion://docs/notion-flavored-markdown-spec` through your MCP client's resource-reading interface, or call the Notion "fetch" tool with this URI if your client does not support reading MCP resources. Do NOT pass this URI to any other URL-fetching tool. Do NOT guess or hallucinate Markdown syntax. Do not put the page title at the top of content; set it in properties. By default, use native Notion mentions for references you add to existing Notion pages, databases, data sources, people, and dates. Use Markdown links only for external URLs or when the user requests a plain link. For a person, use a user mention with their user URL, found with search using query_type "user"; do not write "@Name" as plain text. For a specific date or time, such as a due date or meeting time, use a date mention. The Markdown specification gives the mention syntax.

Use a named destination as parent. Otherwise use "creation_mode": "draft" for a durable private page. Do not combine draft mode with parent, or move or share it without direction.

For a meeting note, use create_meeting_note if available, even in a Meetings database, unless the user wants a regular page.

For a database destination, ALWAYS fetch first. Use its collection:// URL as data_source_id, exact property names, and title property. Never put a database ID in page_id. Outside a database, the only allowed property is the required "title".

For reusable instructions, set "is_skill": true. Before creating a skill, read the MCP resource `notion://docs/skills` through your MCP client's resource-reading interface. If your client does not support reading MCP resources, call the Notion "fetch" tool with this URI instead. Do NOT pass this URI to any other URL-fetching tool. Do not mark ordinary pages or drafts as skills. Report any "warnings" in the result to the user.

properties.description:
The properties of the new page, which is a JSON map of property names to SQLite values.
For pages in a database, use the SQLite schema definition shown in <database>.
For pages outside of a database, the only allowed property is "title", which is the title of the page and is automatically shown at the top of the page as a large heading.
**IMPORTANT**: Some property types require specific formats:
- Date properties: Split into "date:{property}:start", "date:{property}:end" (optional), and "date:{property}:is_datetime" (0 or 1)
- Place properties: Split into "place:{property}:name", "place:{property}:address", "place:{property}:latitude", "place:{property}:longitude", and "place:{property}:google_place_id" (optional)
- Number properties: Use JavaScript numbers (not strings)
- Checkbox properties: Use "__YES__" for checked, "__NO__" for unchecked
- Relation properties: Use an array of related page URLs or page IDs, e.g. ["https://www.notion.so/[redacted]", "26ab1f9f-4c5f-80b1-8d3b-d10a6b1d2f4e"]
- Person properties: Use an array of user IDs, user or agent URLs, or group references copied from fetch output ("space_permission_group-<UUID>"). Bare group UUIDs are also supported.
- Files properties: Use a JSON array of file IDs, Notion Folder URLs, and/or <folder> tags copied from fetch output. Folders are stored as native Folder references, not ordinary links.


**Special property naming**: Properties named "id" or "url" (case insensitive) must be prefixed with "userDefined:" (e.g., "userDefined:URL", "userDefined:id")

content.description: The content of the new page, using Notion Markdown. For people and dates, use user and date mentions rather than plain text; notion://docs/notion-flavored-markdown-spec gives the syntax.

template_id.description: The ID of a template to apply to this page. When specified, do not provide 'content' as the template will provide it. Properties can still be set alongside the template. Get template IDs from the <templates> section in the fetch tool results. Template application is asynchronous: the page starts blank and content appears shortly after.

icon.description: An emoji character (e.g. "🚀"), a custom emoji by name (e.g. ":rocket_ship:"), a Notion icon identifier as returned by fetch (e.g. "icons/pizza_blue"), or an external image URL. Use "none" to explicitly set no icon. Omit to leave unchanged. Keep the title free of a duplicate leading emoji because the icon renders separately.

cover.description: An external image URL for the page cover. Use "none" to explicitly set no cover. Omit to leave unchanged.

is_skill.description: Set to true only when the user asks for reusable instructions or a repeatable workflow. Do not mark ordinary reference pages, one-time documents, or drafts as skills. Before creating a skill, read the MCP resource `notion://docs/skills` through your MCP client's resource-reading interface. If your client does not support reading MCP resources, call the Notion "fetch" tool with this URI instead. Do NOT pass this URI to any other URL-fetching tool. False has the same effect as omitting the field.

preserve_internal_links.description: Preserve internal Markdown links instead of converting them to native mentions.

creation_mode.description: If the user explicitly names a private or shared destination, omit "creation_mode" and use that parent. Otherwise, use "draft" when the user clearly wants a durable page but has not named a destination. Prefer this explicit draft mode over omitting the parent. Draft mode is server-enforced: it creates a private workspace-level page and cannot be combined with "parent". Create it without first asking where it should live. After creation, tell the user it is private and offer to move it once they name a destination.

parent.description: All pages in one call share this parent. Pass "memory" to save a personal memory; see notion://docs/memory. Otherwise use a page (page_id), database page (database_id), data source (data_source_id), or teamspace root (teamspace_id, from get_teams). Teamspace roots require a user-backed connection and permission to add top-level pages. A database_id cannot be used when the database has more than one data source; fetch it and use the right collection:// URL as data_source_id. If omitted, pages are private at the workspace level. When no destination is named, prefer explicit "creation_mode": "draft" over omitting the parent.

page_id.description: The ID of the parent page (with or without dashes), for example, [redacted]

type.description: Always `page_id`

database_id.description: The ID of the parent database (with or without dashes), for example, [redacted]

type.description: Always `database_id`

data_source_id.description: The ID of the parent data source (collection), with or without dashes. For example, f336d0bc-b841-465b-8045-024475c079dd

type.description: Always `data_source_id`

teamspace_id.description: The ID of the teamspace in which to create top-level pages (with or without dashes).

allow_async.description: Default to true for page creation. Set to false only when the next step needs the created pages immediately, or when async execution rejects the request as too large. When this create operation is accepted for background execution, it returns an async_task result. Use get_async_task to wait for a succeeded status before taking a dependent action on the pages. For pages created with template_id, a succeeded status does not mean template content is ready; fetch and retry until it is ready before changing or relying on that content. If omitted or false, the tool keeps the existing synchronous result shape.

instructions_version.description: Notion setup instructions version, such as 0.0.2. Omit if unknown.

tools.name: mcp__plugin_design_notion__notion-fetch
tools.description:
Retrieves details about a Notion entity (page, database, data source, or saved database view) by URL or ID.

Provide a URL or ID in `id`. Make multiple calls for multiple entities.

For pages, use path, verification, edit time, and truncation metadata to assess the source. Treat recency as context, not proof. Report material uncertainty when sources conflict.

Pages use Notion-flavored Markdown. For the complete specification, read the MCP resource `notion://docs/notion-flavored-markdown-spec` through your MCP client's resource-reading interface, or call the Notion "fetch" tool with this URI if your client does not support reading MCP resources. Do NOT pass this URI to any other URL-fetching tool.

Pass a `notion://docs/*` URI as `id` to read that MCP documentation resource.

Databases return data sources in `<data-source url="collection://...">` tags. Fetch the collection:// URL for its schema and use it with update_data_source or query_data_sources. Multi-source databases return more than one data source.

Saved views return filters, sorts, and display settings. To query their rows, use query_data_sources with `mode: "view"`.

A null cover or icon means none; an omitted one means unavailable, not absent. Keep a page's Markdown icon attribute for edit round trips. File URLs expire; re-fetch to refresh them. Uploaded media blocks use stable `notion-file-block://` sources; keep them when editing or copying Markdown. Get download URLs with get_file_download_urls, or set `include_file_urls` to true for a `references` map. Before relying on page content, check `truncated`, `unknown_block_count`, and `unknown_block_ids` for omitted subtrees.

Set `include_discussions` to true for discussion counts, markers, previews, and `discussion://` URLs that correlate with get_comments.

Use get_tool_access to check tool availability, parameter restrictions, and upgrade links for this connection.

id.description: The ID or URL of the Notion page, database, or data source to fetch. Supports notion.so URLs, Notion Sites URLs (*.notion.site), raw UUIDs, and data source URLs (collection://...). Pass "memory" to fetch the connected user's About page and memory database in this workspace without creating them. Pass a notion://docs/* URI to read that documentation resource. Also accepts an explicit saved view URL (view://...) from a database response. If a database block ID returns a validation error, use the collection:// URL from that error. Example: <example>notion://docs/notion-flavored-markdown-spec</example>.

include_transcript.description: Whether to include meeting note transcripts. Defaults to false. When true, full transcripts are included; when false, a placeholder with the meeting note URL is shown instead.

include_discussions.description: Whether to include discussion/comment indicators in the page output. When true, adds a <page-discussions> summary with discussion count, preview snippets, and discussion:// URLs. Use with the get_comments tool to retrieve full discussion content. Defaults to false.

include_file_urls.description: Whether to return signed download URLs for uploaded files. Defaults to false. When false, page Markdown cites uploaded files by stable notion-file-block:// references and the response has no references map; call get_file_download_urls with the references when you need those files' contents. When true, the response's references map gives the signed URL for each reference.

instructions_version.description: Notion setup instructions version, such as 0.0.2. Omit if unknown.

tools.name: mcp__plugin_design_notion__notion-search
tools.description:
Search Notion pages and databases, or look up a user by name or email. Does not search connected apps; use connector_search, when listed, for sources such as Slack, Google Drive, GitHub, mail, or calendar. When connector_search is listed, call it in parallel with search on the first search for an information need, unless the user names a source, the request is a user lookup, or the request is about Notion pages or databases themselves, such as finding a page to read or edit. Decisions, status updates, and discussions often live in connected sources. Preserve distinctive names and identifiers.

Use a non-empty query for content searches. Leave the query empty only when you also send filters or a non-relevance sort, as in the browse example below. Omit optional parameters unless needed. Do not add filters or sorting just to fill in defaults. Business or Enterprise is required for filters.edited_by_user_ids, filters.last_edited_date_range, filters.title_only=true, filters.content_status, more than one distinct teamspace across teamspace_id and filters.teamspace_ids, and sort other than relevance. On other plans, those options are dropped with a notice in the result, and results may be broader. Keep filters nested inside "filters". Use page_size, not limit.

For user lookup, set query_type="user" and provide a name or email. A document about a person is a content search, not a user lookup.

<example description="Find a page by title">
{"query":"Q3 roadmap"}
</example>
<example description="Browse pages you edited most recently">
{"query":"","filters":{"edited_by_user_ids":["me"]},"sort":"last_edited"}
</example>
<example description="Find a user">
{"query":"[redacted]","query_type":"user"}
</example>

query.description: Short, specific keywords for Notion content search. For user search, enter a name or email address. Provide a non-empty query unless intentionally browsing with filters or a non-relevance sort.

query_type.description: Specify type of the query as either "internal" or "user". Always include this input if performing "user" search.

data_source_url.description: Optionally restrict keyword search to a data source URL returned in a <data-source> tag.

page_url.description: Optionally restrict keyword search to a page and its descendants. Accepts a Notion page URL or ID.

teamspace_id.description: Optionally, provide the ID of a teamspace to restrict search results to. This will perform a search over content within the specified teamspace only. Accepts the teamspace ID (UUIDv4) with or without dashes.

filters.description: Optional exact filters for Notion workspace search. Omit unless required by the request. Keep filter fields nested here; do not send them at the top level. Some filters require Business access.

created_date_range.description: Optional filter to only produce search results created within the specified date range.

start_date.description: The start date of the date range as an ISO 8601 date string, if any.

end_date.description: The end date of the date range as an ISO 8601 date string, if any.

created_by_user_ids.description: Optional filter to only produce search results created by the Notion users that have the specified user IDs. Use "me" for the connected user.

edited_by_user_ids.description: Optional filter to only produce search results edited by the Notion users that have the specified user IDs. Use "me" for the connected user. Available on the Business plan.

last_edited_date_range.description: Optional filter to only produce search results last edited within the specified date range. Available on the Business plan.

start_date.description: The start date of the date range as an ISO 8601 date string, if any.

end_date.description: The end date of the date range as an ISO 8601 date string, if any.

teamspace_ids.description: Optional filter to only produce search results inside one of the specified teamspaces. Selecting more than one teamspace is available on the Business plan; use teamspace_id for one teamspace on other plans.

title_only.description: When true, match the query only against page and database titles instead of page content. Available on the Business plan.

content_status.description: Which pages to include by status. Omit for the default live pages. Supplying this field, even with the default value, requires Business access.

sort.description: Result ordering for Notion workspace search. Omit for the default "relevance" ordering. "last_edited" and "created" require Business access.

page_size.description: Maximum number of results to return (default 10). Lower values reduce response size.

max_highlight_length.description: Maximum character length for result highlights (default 200). Set to 0 to omit highlights entirely.

instructions_version.description: Notion setup instructions version, such as 0.0.2. Omit if unknown.

tools.name: DeferredToolPlaceholder
tools.description: Reserved placeholder that keeps deferred tool loading active; never call this tool.

tools.name: mcp__plugin_design_notion__notion-update-page
tools.description:
Update a Notion page's properties, content, icon, or cover. For only an icon or cover, use "update_properties" without "properties".

## Core rules

**IMPORTANT**: Before writing page content, read the MCP resource `notion://docs/notion-flavored-markdown-spec` through your MCP client's resource-reading interface, or call the Notion "fetch" tool with this URI if your client does not support reading MCP resources. Do NOT pass this URI to any other URL-fetching tool. Don't guess Markdown syntax. By default, use native Notion mentions for references you add to existing Notion pages, databases, data sources, people, and dates. Use Markdown links only for external URLs or when the user requests a plain link. For a person, use a user mention with their user URL, found with search using query_type "user"; do not write "@Name" as plain text. For a specific date or time, such as a due date or meeting time, use a date mention. The Markdown specification gives the mention syntax.

Before changing content, fetch unless already loaded. Match nearby headings, block types, nesting, lists, tables, and prose style.

Make the smallest edit. Use "update_content" for targeted search-and-replace and "insert_content" only to prepend or append. Avoid "replace_content" when a targeted command works. Preserve unrelated wording, structure, order, and native references. Do not broadly rewrite unless asked.

For "update_content", use the smallest exact old_str that uniquely matches the target. Ask before removing material content the user did not identify. Don't fetch just to verify an update that completed without warnings. Fetch to resolve warnings, or when a later step needs the page's exact saved state.

For "replace_content", preserve child pages and databases with their exact fetched tags. If validation says child content would be deleted, show the list and ask first. Never retry with "allow_deleting_content": true without confirmation. Report any "warnings" in the result.

page_id.description: The page ID, with or without dashes, or a Notion page URL.

properties.description:
Used by the "update_properties" command, and required unless "icon", "cover", or "is_skill" is set. A JSON object that updates the page's properties.
For pages in a database, fetch the page or its data source first and use the exact property names and SQLite schema definition shown in <database>.
For pages outside of a database, the only allowed property is "title", which is the title of the page in inline markdown format.
For a Files property, an uploaded file can be provided as {"type":"file_upload","file_upload":{"id":"<file-upload-id>"}} inside the property's array.
Use null to remove a property's value.

Use Markdown links only for external URLs or when the user requests a plain link. For a person, use a user mention with their user URL, found with search using query_type "user"; do not write "@Name" as plain text. content.text:
Yes. There are two separate problems behind "loads too much", and each has its own fix.

**1. `/continue` does all the work when you type it**
Right now `/continue` reads the whole previous session log from start to finish every time.

**Fix: keep the summary saved and up to date as you work.** Add a Claude Code hook that runs after every reply (the `Stop` hook). It reads only the new lines added since last time and updates a saved summary file for the project, e.g. `~/.footprint/state/<project>.md`. Then `/continue` just prints that file. It's instant, and the summary stays current while you work. This is the "continuous caching" you're describing.

**2. Too much text gets pasted in**
`/continue` pastes about 1k tokens (4000 characters) whether the model needs it or not.

**Fix: paste a short version and look up the rest on demand.**
- `/continue` gives only about 150 tokens: the goal, where you stopped, and the open todos.
- footprint also runs as an MCP server with tools like `footprint_context("files touched")` and `footprint_context("last error")`. The model calls these only when it needs the detail.
- OpenCode supports MCP, so this works there too, and later in the VS Code wrapper.

**What "caching" can't do here**
- **Claude's prompt caching** only reuses text sent to Claude itself. When you switch to OpenCode with Big Pickle, nothing is reused. It doesn't help when moving between tools.
- **Cache inside the footprint model:** `mlx_lm server` can keep a long shared start of the prompt in memory, so it isn't processed again on each request. That only matters if you use the local footprint model and give it large context.

**My recommendation:** build fix 1 now; it's about 30 lines. Then fix 2, which is a small MCP server and gets more value from fewer tokens. Together they give a summary that's always ready, a small paste, and details only when needed. That fits "X× cheaper" too, because fewer tokens are spent on context.

Build fix 1 now?

input.content: ## Problems right now Keep these in mind — what we're going through with continuity v1. ### P1. /continue does all the work on demand - Every /continue re-reads and parses the entire previous transcript from scratch. Grows slower as sessions get long. - Fix (planned) — continuous caching: a Claude Code Stop hook (fires after every reply) incrementally parses only new transcript lines (byte offset) and keeps a per-project state file always current (e.g. ~/.footprint/state/<project>.md). /continue just reads it → instant, always fresh. ~30 lines. ### P2. Too much context loaded at once - /continue injects the full ~1k-token state whether the model needs it or not. Hurts the \"fraction of the cost\" story. - Fix (planned) — small summary + lazy lookup: inject only ~150 tokens (goal, where it stopped, open todos). Expose footprint as an MCP server with tools like footprint_context(\"files touched\") / footprint_context(\"last error\") so the agent pulls details only when needed. Works in OpenCode and later the VS Code wrapper. ### P3. Caching across tools isn't free - Claude prompt caching only helps when the next call goes to Claude again. Switching to OpenCode / Big Pickle = different provider = no cache reuse. - Only place KV/prompt caching helps us: our own local model (mlx_lm server prompt cache reuse for a shared context prefix). ### P4. OpenCode is manual + one-way - OpenCode needs /continue typed by hand (auto needs an OpenCode plugin). - OpenCode sessions (~/.local/share/opencode) aren't read back, so switching OpenCode → Claude loses that work. ### P5. content.text:
No. For what you're building now, the Qwen training isn't needed, and it doesn't support the pitch.

**The continuity feature doesn't use Qwen at all.** `footprint context` just reads the session logs and writes a summary, with no model involved. That summary goes to whatever model the tool already uses: Claude, Big Pickle in OpenCode, GPT in Cursor. The product people get value from is the context layer, and it works with any model.

**What training Qwen actually gives you:**
- A 1.5B model that copies how your sessions look: their tone, and the format of tool calls.
- Training on your sessions teaches style. It doesn't teach the model to code better. A 1.5B model won't come anywhere near Opus 5.5 at coding, no matter how much you train it.
- It runs free, offline and privately. That part is real, but it's only useful if the model is good enough for the job.

**It works against your claims:**
- "As good as Opus 5.5" can only come from a strong model plus good context, e.g. Big Pickle or Claude with footprint's summary. It can't come from the Qwen model.
- "X× cheaper" comes from not paying to rebuild context, plus using a cheaper model. Qwen isn't part of that.

**Where a small local model still makes sense:** as a helper behind the scenes, not as the coding agent.
- **Shrinking context:** turning long sessions into the ~150-token summary from P2. Small models handle that fine, it costs nothing, and the text never leaves the machine.
- **Enterprise:** summaries made on the company's own hardware, so session logs never go to an outside API. That's a selling point for the business tier.
- **Searching past work:** finding the right earlier session or detail when the model asks over MCP.

**My recommendation:**
1. Make footprint the context layer that works with any model. That's the main product.
2. Keep `train` and `serve` as optional experimental features. Stop leading with them in the README and on the site.
3. Later, use a small local model as the summarizer for P2 and the enterprise tier, not as the coding agent.

We also never ran `footprint eval` on a trained model, so we have no evidence it helps. That makes it even less worth leading with.

content.text:
Partly. A model can learn how Opus works in your projects, but it can't learn how well Opus reasons.

**What can carry over to another model:**
- **Project knowledge:** naming conventions, which commands work, which files matter, decisions already made, known pitfalls. Much of what makes Opus look smart in your repo is this, and any model can use it if you give it to it.
- **Working method:** read the code before editing, plan, run tests, make small changes, then summarize. A weaker model can follow these steps when they're spelled out.
- **Tool use:** how and when to call each tool.

**What can't carry over:** reasoning ability. Finding subtle bugs, multi-step debugging, and long tasks depend on how strong the model is. Context and training data don't close that gap.

**Ways to do it, best value first:**
1. **Extract a playbook (cheap, works with any model).** footprint reads your Claude sessions and writes `AGENTS.md` plus skills: conventions, commands, decisions, how-to steps. OpenCode and Cursor read `AGENTS.md` automatically. This builds on what `context` already does.
2. **Show past examples.** For a new task, find a similar past Opus session and paste in how Opus solved it ("last time a bug like this, Opus checked X, then fixed Y"). Weaker models improve a lot from examples.
3. **Router (the honest way to get Opus-level results).** A cheap model handles routine steps and hands hard ones to Opus. Results stay at Opus quality on the parts that need it, and cost drops on everything else. This is the realistic path to "X× cheaper, as good as Opus."
4. **Checking loop.** Tests and linters catch the weaker model's mistakes automatically.
5. **Training a model on Opus sessions.** This is what `footprint train` does today. It works better with bigger models, e.g. Qwen 32B rather than 1.5B, and thousands of tasks. It transfers style and tool use, not reasoning.

**Legal warning about option 5:** Anthropic's terms prohibit using Claude's outputs to build or train competing AI models. Training a model on Opus sessions and selling it, especially to businesses, could break those terms. Get a legal review before doing this commercially. Options 1–4 use your project knowledge as context, which is the normal intended use, so they carry far less of this risk.

**My recommendation:** do options 1, 2 and 3. The pitch then becomes "Opus results at a fraction of the cost: any model gets your project's playbook, and only the hard parts go to Opus." That's a claim you can defend. "Model X equals Opus 5.5" isn't.

content.content:
# footprint

**Your Claude, learned locally.**

Footprint watches your Claude Code sessions, fine-tunes a small local model
(LoRA) on how *you and Claude* work in your projects, and serves it as an
OpenAI-compatible API. When your Claude quota runs out, OpenCode (or Cursor,
or Codex CLI) keeps working in the same style — fully offline, on your machine.

```
trace → chat with claude → collect → train → install → /footprint in OpenCode
```

## How it works

1. Claude Code already logs every session (prompts, replies, tool calls) to `~/.claude/projects`.
2. `footprint trace` arms a marker so only sessions from that point on become training data.
3. `footprint collect` parses those transcripts into chat-format training examples.
4. `footprint train` LoRA fine-tunes a small model (default: Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B, 4-bit MLX) on them.
5. `footprint install` registers a launchd agent — the server runs itself at
   `http://127.0.0.1:8399/v1`, starts at login, restarts on crash. You never run it by hand.
6. Any OpenAI-compatible tool points at that URL and behaves like your Claude.

## Requirements

| | trace / collect | train / serve |
|---|---|---|
| **macOS (Apple Silicon)** | ✅ | ✅ MLX backend |
| **Linux** | ✅ | ✅ torch backend (CUDA or CPU) |
| **Windows** | ✅ | ✅ torch backend (CUDA or CPU) |
| **macOS (Intel)** | ✅ | ✅ torch backend (CPU) |

- [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) installed and used at least once
- Python 3.9+
- Node.js 18+ (only if installing via npm)

footprint picks the backend automatically: [MLX](https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx)
on Apple Silicon, PyTorch + PEFT everywhere else (uses CUDA when available;
CPU works but trains slowly — prefer a GPU or drop `FOOTPRINT_ITERS`).

## Install

### macOS

```sh
npm install -g footprint-trace
```

or from source:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/Amanlabh/footprint.git
cd footprint
python3 footprint.py setup
```

### Linux

```sh
npm install -g footprint-trace      # or the git clone above
```

First run installs the torch backend (one-time, ~2 GB). CUDA GPU picked up automatically.

### Windows

Use PowerShell (Python 3 from python.org or the Microsoft Store):

```powershell
npm install -g footprint-trace
```

Same as Linux: full trace/collect/train/serve via the torch backend. WSL2 also works.

## Getting started

**1. Arm tracing — before you start Claude.**

```sh
footprint trace
```

Claude Code already logs every session; the trace marker makes footprint train
only on sessions from this point on. (Skip this step — or delete
`~/.claude/footprint-trace` — to train on your entire history instead.)

**2. Use Claude Code normally.**

```sh
claude
```

Every session (your prompts, Claude's replies, tool calls) is captured automatically.

**3. Collect and train.**

```sh
footprint collect     # transcripts -> data/train.jsonl + data/valid.jsonl
footprint train       # LoRA fine-tune (~10 min, downloads ~1 GB base model first time)
```

**4. Install the always-on server.**

```sh
footprint install
```

This registers the server with your OS — launchd (macOS), systemd (Linux) or
Task Scheduler (Windows) — so it starts at login, restarts if it crashes, and
you never run it by hand. It also wires up OpenCode:

- provider `footprint` at `http://127.0.0.1:8399/v1`
- a `/footprint <task>` command inside OpenCode

**5. Claude quota over? Keep going.**

Open OpenCode and type:

```
/footprint fix the failing test in auth.py
```

Or point any OpenAI-compatible tool at the server:

| Tool | Setting |
|---|---|
| **Cursor** | Settings → Models → OpenAI base URL `http://127.0.0.1:8399/v1`, any API key, add model `footprint` |
| **Codex CLI** | custom provider with that base URL in `~/.codex/config.toml` |
| **anything else** | base URL `http://127.0.0.1:8399/v1`, API key: none |

| **Linux** | ✅ | ✅ torch backend (CUDA or CPU) |
| **Windows** | ✅ | ✅ torch backend (CUDA or CPU) |
| **macOS (Intel)** | ✅ | ✅ torch backend (CPU) |

- [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) installed and used at least once
- Python 3.9+
- Node.js 18+ (only if installing via npm)

footprint picks the backend automatically: [MLX](https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx)
on Apple Silicon, PyTorch + PEFT everywhere else (uses CUDA when available;
CPU works but trains slowly — prefer a GPU or drop `FOOTPRINT_ITERS`).

## Install

### macOS

```sh
npm install -g footprint-trace
```

or from source:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/Amanlabh/footprint.git
cd footprint
python3 footprint.py setup
```

### Linux

```sh
npm install -g footprint-trace      # or the git clone above
```

First run installs the torch backend (one-time, ~2 GB). CUDA GPU picked up automatically.

### Windows

Use PowerShell (Python 3 from python.org or the Microsoft Store):

```powershell
npm install -g footprint-trace
```

Same as Linux: full trace/collect/train/serve via the torch backend. WSL2 also works.

## Getting started

**1. Arm tracing — before you start Claude.**

```sh
footprint trace
```

Claude Code already logs every session; the trace marker makes footprint train
only on sessions from this point on. (Skip this step — or delete
`~/.claude/footprint-trace` — to train on your entire history instead.)

**2. Use Claude Code normally.**

```sh
claude
```

Every session (your prompts, Claude's replies, tool calls) is captured automatically.

**3. Collect and train.**

```sh
footprint collect     # transcripts -> data/train.jsonl + data/valid.jsonl
footprint train       # LoRA fine-tune (~10 min, downloads ~1 GB base model first time)
```

**4. Install the always-on server.**

```sh
footprint install
```

This registers the server with your OS — launchd (macOS), systemd (Linux) or
Task Scheduler (Windows) — so it starts at login, restarts if it crashes, and
you never run it by hand. It also wires up OpenCode:

- provider `footprint` at `http://127.0.0.1:8399/v1`
- a `/footprint <task>` command inside OpenCode

**5. Claude quota over? Keep going.**

Open OpenCode and type:

```
/footprint fix the failing test in auth.py
```

Or point any OpenAI-compatible tool at the server:

| Tool | Setting |
|---|---|
| **Cursor** | Settings → Models → OpenAI base URL `http://127.0.0.1:8399/v1`, any API key, add model `footprint` |
| **Codex CLI** | custom provider with that base URL in `~/.codex/config.toml` |
| **anything else** | base URL `http://127.0.0.1:8399/v1`, API key: none |

1	"""Session continuity: hand a new Claude Code session the state of the previous one.
2	
3	Claude Code writes transcripts live, so "real-time" needs no daemon: at
4	SessionStart we read the newest other transcript in the project and print a
5	compact state (goal, files touched, open todos, last error, where it ended).
6	Hook stdout becomes context for the new session.
7	"""
8	import glob, json, os, sys, time
9	
10	from . import config, transcripts
11	
12	EDIT_TOOLS = {"Edit", "Write", "MultiEdit", "NotebookEdit"}
13	
14	
15	def _prompt(rec):
16	    """Real user prompt text, or None for tool results / meta / slash-command noise."""
17	    if rec.get("type") != "user" or rec.get("isMeta") or rec.get("isSidechain"):
18	        return None
19	    c = (rec.get("message") or {}).get("content")
20	    if isinstance(c, list) and any(b.get("type") == "tool_result" for b in c):
21	        return None
22	    t = transcripts._text(c)
23	    return None if not t or t.startswith("<command-") else t
24	
25	
26	def state(path):
27	    """One transcript -> dict of what a successor session needs to know."""
28	    s = {"title": None, "prompts": [], "files": [], "todos": None, "error": None,
29	         "last": None, "branch": None, "cwd": None}
30	    for line in open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"):
31	        try:
32	            rec = json.loads(line)
33	        except json.JSONDecodeError:
34	            continue
35	        if rec.get("type") == "ai-title":
36	            s["title"] = rec.get("aiTitle")
37	        s["branch"] = rec.get("gitBranch") or s["branch"]
38	        s["cwd"] = rec.get("cwd") or s["cwd"]
39	        p = _prompt(rec)
40	        if p:
41	            s["prompts"].append(p)
42	        content = (rec.get("message") or {}).get("content")
43	        if rec.get("isSidechain") or not isinstance(content, list):
44	            continue
45	        for b in content:
46	            if b.get("type") == "tool_use":
47	                inp = b.get("input") or {}
48	                f = inp.get("file_path") or inp.get("notebook_path")
49	                if b.get("name") in EDIT_TOOLS and f:
50	                    if f in s["files"]:
51	                        s["files"].remove(f)
52	                    s["files"].append(f)  # most recent last
53	                elif b.get("name") == "TodoWrite":
54	                    s["todos"] = [t for t in inp.get("todos", []) if t.get("status") != "completed"]
55	            elif b.get("type") == "tool_result" and b.get("is_error"):
56	                s["error"] = transcripts._text([b], cap=400)
57	            elif b.get("type") == "text" and rec.get("type") == "assistant" and b["text"].strip():
58	                s["last"] = b["text"].strip()
59	    return s
60	
61	
62	def render(s, age_h):
63	    out = [f"# Previous session in this project (last active {age_h:.1f}h ago"
64	           + (f", branch {s['branch']}" if s["branch"] else "") + ")"]
65	    if s["title"]:
66	        out.append(f"Topic: {s['title']}")
67	    out.append(f"Goal (first ask): {s['prompts'][0][:600]}")
68	    if len(s["prompts"]) > 1:
69	        out.append("Latest asks:\n" + "\n".join(f"- {p[:300]}" for p in s["prompts"][-3:]))
70	    if s["files"]:
71	        out.append("Files touched: " + ", ".join(s["files"][-15:]))
72	    if s["todos"]:
73	        out.append("Open todos:\n" + "\n".join(f"- [{t.get('status')}] {t.get('content')}" for t in s["todos"]))
74	    if s["error"]:
75	        out.append(f"Last tool error (may be resolved): {s['error']}")
76	    if s["last"]:
77	        out.append(f"Where it ended:\n{s['last'][-800:]}")
78	    out.append("Continue from here if the user's next request relates; don't re-ask what's above.")
79	    return "\n\n".join(out)[:config.CONTEXT_CAP]
80	
81	
82	def previous(project_dir, current=None):
83	    """Newest transcript in project_dir that isn't the current session and has a real prompt."""
84	    for f in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(project_dir, "*.jsonl")), key=os.path.getmtime, reverse=True):
85	        if current and os.path.basename(f) == f"{current}.jsonl":
86	            continue
87	        age_h = (time.time() - os.path.getmtime(f)) / 3600
88	        if age_h > config.CONTEXT_MAX_AGE_H:
89	            return None  # sorted newest-first: everything after is staler
90	        s = state(f)
91	        if s["prompts"]:
92	            return s, age_h
93	    return None

97	    """`footprint context` — print previous-session state. As a SessionStart hook,
98	    reads the hook JSON from stdin; by hand, uses the current directory."""
99	    if args and args[0] == "install":
100	        return install()
101	    hook = {}
102	    if not sys.stdin.isatty():
103	        try:
104	            hook = json.loads(sys.stdin.read() or "{}")
105	        except json.JSONDecodeError:
106	            pass
107	    tp = hook.get("transcript_path")
108	    pdir = os.path.dirname(tp) if tp else transcripts.project_dir(hook.get("cwd") or os.getcwd())
109	    found = previous(pdir, hook.get("session_id"))
110	    if found:
111	        print(render(*found))
112	    elif not hook:
113	        print(f"no previous session within {config.CONTEXT_MAX_AGE_H}h in {pdir}")
114

116	def install():
117	    """Register `footprint context` as a Claude Code SessionStart hook (startup + /clear)."""
118	    path = os.path.expanduser("~/.claude/settings.json")
119	    try:
120	        cfg = json.load(open(path, encoding="utf-8")) if os.path.exists(path) else {}
121	    except json.JSONDecodeError:
122	        sys.exit(f"{path} is not valid JSON — fix it first, not overwriting")
123	    cmd = f'"{sys.executable}" "{config.ENTRY}" context'
124	    starts = cfg.setdefault("hooks", {}).setdefault("SessionStart", [])
125	    starts[:] = [e for e in starts if not any("footprint.py\" context" in h.get("command", "")
126	                                              for h in e.get("hooks", []))]
127	    starts.append({"matcher": "startup|clear", "hooks": [{"type": "command", "command": cmd}]})
128	    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(path), exist_ok=True)

130	        json.dump(cfg, f, indent=2)
131	    # ponytail: OpenCode gets a manual /continue (shell-output injection); auto needs an OpenCode plugin
132	    oc = os.path.join(config.OPENCODE, "commands", "continue.md")
133	    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(oc), exist_ok=True)
134	    with open(oc, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:

"""Session continuity: hand a new session the state of the previous one.

Works across tools: the previous session is the newest one for this project in
either Claude Code (~/.claude/projects/*.jsonl) or OpenCode (opencode.db).
Both write live, so "real-time" needs no daemon: at session start we read the
newest other session and print a compact state (goal, files touched, open
todos, last error, where it ended). Claude Code gets it via a SessionStart
hook, OpenCode via a plugin (plus /continue for existing sessions).
"""
import glob, json, os, shutil, sqlite3, sys, time

from . import config, transcripts

EDIT_TOOLS = {"Edit", "Write", "MultiEdit", "NotebookEdit", "edit", "write"}
DONE = {"completed", "cancelled"}
HANDOFF_END = "Continue from here if the user's next request relates; don't re-ask what's above."
PLUGIN_SRC = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "opencode_plugin.js")


def _new_state(src, **kw):
    return {"src": src, "title": None, "prompts": [], "files": [], "todos": None, "error": None,
            "last": None, "branch": None, "cwd": None, **kw}


def _touch(files, f):
    if f in files:
        files.remove(f)
    files.append(f)  # most recent last


def _strip_handoff(t):
    """Drop a footprint handoff block pasted in by /continue; keep the user's own words after it."""
    return t.split(HANDOFF_END, 1)[1].strip() if HANDOFF_END in t else t


def _prompt(rec):
    """Real user prompt text, or None for tool results / meta / slash-command noise."""
    if rec.get("type") != "user" or rec.get("isMeta") or rec.get("isSidechain"):
        return None
    c = (rec.get("message") or {}).get("content")
    if isinstance(c, list) and any(b.get("type") == "tool_result" for b in c):
        return None
    t = _strip_handoff(transcripts._text(c))
    return None if not t or t.startswith("<command-") else t


def state(path):
    """One Claude Code transcript -> dict of what a successor session needs to know."""
    s = _new_state("Claude Code")
    for line in open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"):
        try:
            rec = json.loads(line)
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            continue
        if rec.get("type") == "ai-title":
            s["title"] = rec.get("aiTitle")
        s["branch"] = rec.get("gitBranch") or s["branch"]
        s["cwd"] = rec.get("cwd") or s["cwd"]
        p = _prompt(rec)
        if p:
            s["prompts"].append(p)
        content = (rec.get("message") or {}).get("content")
        if rec.get("isSidechain") or not isinstance(content, list):
            continue
        for b in content:
            if b.get("type") == "tool_use":
                inp = b.get("input") or {}
                f = inp.get("file_path") or inp.get("notebook_path")
                if b.get("name") in EDIT_TOOLS and f:
                    _touch(s["files"], f)
                elif b.get("name") == "TodoWrite":
                    s["todos"] = [t for t in inp.get("todos", []) if t.get("status") not in DONE]
            elif b.get("type") == "tool_result" and b.get("is_error"):
                s["error"] = transcripts._text([b], cap=400)
            elif b.get("type") == "text" and rec.get("type") == "assistant" and b["text"].strip():
                s["last"] = b["text"].strip()
    return s


def claude_previous(project_dir, current=None):
    """Newest Claude transcript in project_dir that isn't the current session and has a real prompt."""
    for f in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(project_dir, "*.jsonl")), key=os.path.getmtime, reverse=True):
        if current and os.path.basename(f) == f"{current}.jsonl":
            continue
        age_h = (time.time() - os.path.getmtime(f)) / 3600
        if age_h > config.CONTEXT_MAX_AGE_H:
            return None  # sorted newest-first: everything after is staler
        s = state(f)
        if s["prompts"]:
            return s, age_h
    return None


def opencode_previous(cwd, current=None):
    """Newest top-level OpenCode session for cwd (not current) -> (state, age_h), or None."""
    if not os.path.exists(config.OPENCODE_DB):
        return None
    try:

newest other session and print a compact state (goal, files touched, open
todos, last error, where it ended). Claude Code gets it via a SessionStart

import glob, json, os, shutil, sqlite3, sys, time

def _new_state(src, **kw):
    return {"src": src, "title": None, "prompts": [], "files": [], "todos": None, "error": None,
            "last": None, "branch": None, "cwd": None, **kw}


def _touch(files, f):
    if f in files:
        files.remove(f)
    files.append(f)  # most recent last

    """Drop a footprint handoff block pasted in by /continue; keep the user's own words after it."""
    return t.split(HANDOFF_END, 1)[1].strip() if HANDOFF_END in t else t

    """Real user prompt text, or None for tool results / meta / slash-command noise."""
    if rec.get("type") != "user" or rec.get("isMeta") or rec.get("isSidechain"):
        return None
    c = (rec.get("message") or {}).get("content")
    if isinstance(c, list) and any(b.get("type") == "tool_result" for b in c):
        return None
    t = _strip_handoff(transcripts._text(c))
    return None if not t or t.startswith("<command-") else t

    """One Claude Code transcript -> dict of what a successor session needs to know."""

            rec = json.loads(line)
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            continue
        if rec.get("type") == "ai-title":
            s["title"] = rec.get("aiTitle")
        s["branch"] = rec.get("gitBranch") or s["branch"]
        s["cwd"] = rec.get("cwd") or s["cwd"]
        p = _prompt(rec)
        if p:
            s["prompts"].append(p)
        content = (rec.get("message") or {}).get("content")
        if rec.get("isSidechain") or not isinstance(content, list):
            continue
        for b in content:
            if b.get("type") == "tool_use":
                inp = b.get("input") or {}
                f = inp.get("file_path") or inp.get("notebook_path")
                if b.get("name") in EDIT_TOOLS and f:
                    _touch(s["files"], f)
                elif b.get("name") == "TodoWrite":

"""Session continuity: hand a new session the state of the previous one.

Works across tools: the previous session is the newest one for this project in
either Claude Code (~/.claude/projects/*.jsonl) or OpenCode (opencode.db).
Both write live, so "real-time" needs no daemon: at session start we read the
newest other session and print a compact state (goal, files touched, open
todos, last error, where it ended). Claude Code gets it via a SessionStart
hook, OpenCode via a plugin (plus /continue for existing sessions).
"""
import glob, json, os, shutil, sqlite3, sys, time

from . import config, transcripts

EDIT_TOOLS = {"Edit", "Write", "MultiEdit", "NotebookEdit", "edit", "write"}
DONE = {"completed", "cancelled"}
HANDOFF_END = "Continue from here if the user's next request relates; don't re-ask what's above."
PLUGIN_SRC = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "opencode_plugin.js")


def _new_state(src, **kw):
    return {"src": src, "title": None, "prompts": [], "files": [], "todos": None, "error": None,
            "last": None, "branch": None, "cwd": None, **kw}


def _touch(files, f):
    if f in files:
        files.remove(f)
    files.append(f)  # most recent last


def _strip_handoff(t):
    """Drop a footprint handoff block pasted in by /continue; keep the user's own words after it."""
    return t.split(HANDOFF_END, 1)[1].strip() if HANDOFF_END in t else t


def _prompt(rec):
    """Real user prompt text, or None for tool results / meta / slash-command noise."""
    if rec.get("type") != "user" or rec.get("isMeta") or rec.get("isSidechain"):
        return None
    c = (rec.get("message") or {}).get("content")
    if isinstance(c, list) and any(b.get("type") == "tool_result" for b in c):
        return None
    t = _strip_handoff(transcripts._text(c))
    return None if not t or t.startswith("<command-") else t


def state(path):
    """One Claude Code transcript -> dict of what a successor session needs to know."""
    s = _new_state("Claude Code")
    for line in open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"):
        try:
            rec = json.loads(line)
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            continue
        if rec.get("type") == "ai-title":
            s["title"] = rec.get("aiTitle")
        s["branch"] = rec.get("gitBranch") or s["branch"]
        s["cwd"] = rec.get("cwd") or s["cwd"]
        p = _prompt(rec)
        if p:
            s["prompts"].append(p)
        content = (rec.get("message") or {}).get("content")
        if rec.get("isSidechain") or not isinstance(content, list):
            continue
        for b in content:
            if b.get("type") == "tool_use":
                inp = b.get("input") or {}
                f = inp.get("file_path") or inp.get("notebook_path")
                if b.get("name") in EDIT_TOOLS and f:
                    _touch(s["files"], f)
                elif b.get("name") == "TodoWrite":
                    s["todos"] = [t for t in inp.get("todos", []) if t.get("status") not in DONE]
            elif b.get("type") == "tool_result" and b.get("is_error"):
                s["error"] = transcripts._text([b], cap=400)
            elif b.get("type") == "text" and rec.get("type") == "assistant" and b["text"].strip():
                s["last"] = b["text"].strip()
    return s


def claude_previous(project_dir, current=None):
    """Newest Claude transcript in project_dir that isn't the current session and has a real prompt."""
    for f in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(project_dir, "*.jsonl")), key=os.path.getmtime, reverse=True):
        if current and os.path.basename(f) == f"{current}.jsonl":
            continue
        age_h = (time.time() - os.path.getmtime(f)) / 3600
        if age_h > config.CONTEXT_MAX_AGE_H:
            return None  # sorted newest-first: everything after is staler
        s = state(f)
        if s["prompts"]:
            return s, age_h
    return None


def opencode_previous(cwd, current=None):
    """Newest top-level OpenCode session for cwd (not current) -> (state, age_h), or None."""
    if not os.path.exists(config.OPENCODE_DB):
        return None
    try:
        db = sqlite3.connect(f"file:{config.OPENCODE_DB}?mode=ro", uri=True)
    except sqlite3.Error:
        return None
    try:
        sessions = db.execute(
            "select id, title, time_updated from session where directory = ? and parent_id is null "
            "and time_archived is null and id != ? order by time_updated desc limit 5",
            (os.path.abspath(cwd), current or "")).fetchall()
        for sid, title, updated in sessions:
            age_h = (time.time() - updated / 1000) / 3600
            if age_h > config.CONTEXT_MAX_AGE_H:
                return None
            s = _new_state("OpenCode", title=title, cwd=cwd)
            roles = {mid: json.loads(d).get("role") for mid, d in
                     db.execute("select id, data from message where session_id = ?", (sid,))}
            for mid, d in db.execute("select message_id, data from part where session_id = ? "
                                     "order by time_created, id", (sid,)):
                p = json.loads(d)
                if p.get("type") == "text" and not p.get("synthetic") and (p.get("text") or "").strip():
                    if roles.get(mid) == "user":
                        t = _strip_handoff(p["text"].strip())
                        if t:
                            s["prompts"].append(t)
                    else:
                        s["last"] = p["text"].strip()
                elif p.get("type") == "tool":
                    st = p.get("state") or {}
                    f = (st.get("input") or {}).get("filePath")
                    if p.get("tool") in EDIT_TOOLS and f:
                        _touch(s["files"], f)
                    if st.get("status") == "error":
                        s["error"] = str(st.get("error") or "")[:400]
            s["todos"] = [{"content": c, "status": st} for c, st in db.execute(
                "select content, status from todo where session_id = ? order by position", (sid,))
                if st not in DONE]
            if s["prompts"]:
                return s, age_h
    except (sqlite3.Error, json.JSONDecodeError):
        return None  # OpenCode schema changed: degrade to Claude-only, never break the hook
    finally:
        db.close()
    return None


def previous(cwd, current=None, project_dir=None):
    """Newest prior session for this project across Claude Code and OpenCode."""
    found = [f for f in (claude_previous(project_dir or transcripts.project_dir(cwd), current),
                         opencode_previous(cwd, current)) if f]
    return min(found, key=lambda f: f[1]) if found else None


def render(s, age_h):
    out = [f"# Previous session in this project ({s['src']}, last active {age_h:.1f}h ago"
           + (f", branch {s['branch']}" if s["branch"] else "") + ")"]
    if s["title"]:
        out.append(f"Topic: {s['title']}")
    out.append(f"Goal (first ask): {s['prompts'][0][:600]}")
    if len(s["prompts"]) > 1:
        out.append("Latest asks:\n" + "\n".join(f"- {p[:300]}" for p in s["prompts"][-3:]))
    if s["files"]:
        out.append("Files touched: " + ", ".join(s["files"][-15:]))
    if s["todos"]:
        out.append("Open todos:\n" + "\n".join(f"- [{t.get('status')}] {t.get('content')}" for t in s["todos"]))
    if s["error"]:
        out.append(f"Last tool error (may be resolved): {s['error']}")
    if s["last"]:
        out.append(f"Where it ended:\n{s['last'][-800:]}")
    out.append(HANDOFF_END)
    return "\n\n".join(out)[:config.CONTEXT_CAP]


def show(args=()):
    """`footprint context` — print previous-session state. As a hook (Claude
    SessionStart or the OpenCode plugin), reads {cwd, session_id, transcript_path?}
    JSON from stdin; by hand, uses the current directory."""
    if args and args[0] == "install":
        return install()
    hook = {}
    if not sys.stdin.isatty():
        try:
            hook = json.loads(sys.stdin.read() or "{}")
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            pass
    tp = hook.get("transcript_path")
    cwd = hook.get("cwd") or os.getcwd()
    found = previous(cwd, hook.get("session_id"), os.path.dirname(tp) if tp else None)
    if found:
        print(render(*found))
    elif not hook:
        print(f"no previous session within {config.CONTEXT_MAX_AGE_H}h for {cwd}")


def install():
    """Claude Code SessionStart hook + OpenCode plugin (auto) + /continue command (manual)."""
    path = os.path.expanduser("~/.claude/settings.json")
    try:
        cfg = json.load(open(path, encoding="utf-8")) if os.path.exists(path) else {}
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        sys.exit(f"{path} is not valid JSON — fix it first, not overwriting")
    cmd = f'"{sys.executable}" "{config.ENTRY}" context'
    starts = cfg.setdefault("hooks", {}).setdefault("SessionStart", [])
    starts[:] = [e for e in starts if not any("footprint.py\" context" in h.get("command", "")
                                              for h in e.get("hooks", []))]
    starts.append({"matcher": "startup|clear", "hooks": [{"type": "command", "command": cmd}]})
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(path), exist_ok=True)
    with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump(cfg, f, indent=2)
    plugin = os.path.join(config.OPENCODE, "plugins", "footprint.js")
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(plugin), exist_ok=True)
    src = open(PLUGIN_SRC, encoding="utf-8").read()
    with open(plugin, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(src.replace("__PY__", json.dumps(sys.executable)).replace("__ENTRY__", json.dumps(config.ENTRY)))
    oc = os.path.join(config.OPENCODE, "commands", "continue.md")
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(oc), exist_ok=True)
    with open(oc, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write("---\ndescription: continue from your last session in this project, Claude Code or OpenCode (footprint)\n---\n"
                f"!`{cmd}`\n\n$ARGUMENTS\n")
    print(f"continuity on — new sessions start where the last one (Claude Code or OpenCode) left off.\n"
          f"  claude code: SessionStart hook (startup|clear) in {path}\n"
          f"  opencode:    auto via plugin {plugin}\n"
          f"               /continue [task] for sessions already open ({oc})\n"
          f"  preview:     footprint context")

content.text:
OpenCode now picks up where you left off without you typing anything, and it works in both directions. I committed it (`70e2b05`), but **the push is stuck** waiting on the macOS keychain. It probably needs you to approve a dialog on screen; if nothing shows up, run `! git push origin main` yourself.

## How it works

```
Claude Code session ─┐                        ┌─► new Claude session   (hook, automatic)
                     ├─► footprint context ───┤
OpenCode session ────┘    picks the newest    └─► new OpenCode session (plugin, automatic)
                          session for this project
```

- **footprint reads both tools.** Claude Code logs are in `~/.claude/projects/*.jsonl`. OpenCode sessions are in `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`, which footprint only reads, never writes. Whichever session is newest for the project gets handed to the next one.
- **The OpenCode plugin** is in `~/.config/opencode/plugins/footprint.js`. When you create a session, it builds the summary once and adds it to that session's system prompt.
  - Built once per session, not every turn, so the system prompt stays identical. That lets the model provider reuse its prompt cache, which partly covers the "continuous caching" idea from P1.
  - Sub-sessions that OpenCode starts for subtasks don't get it, so it doesn't fill their context.
  - If OpenCode changes how it stores sessions, footprint falls back to Claude sessions only. The Claude hook keeps working either way.
- **What the summary contains:** topic, goal, latest requests, files edited, open todos, last error, where it ended, and which tool the session was in. If a session started with `/continue`, the pasted summary is removed first, so it doesn't end up summarized again.

## Tested for real
- **Automatic in OpenCode:** I ran `opencode run` with Big Pickle and typed nothing extra. It correctly described this Claude session: Notion MCP, the continuity work, and ended on the `context.py` rewrite.
- **Reverse direction:** footprint read that real OpenCode session out of the database, with the right title, first request and last reply.
- **Tests:** the built-in check covers the Claude and OpenCode paths, including stripping `/continue` summaries. The pytest suite passes, 3 of 3.

## Get started

**Your machine:** already done. Just open OpenCode in a project:
```bash
cd ~/Developer/footprint && opencode
```
Restart OpenCode if it was already open so it loads the plugin. Choose Big Pickle once with `/models`, then type normally. `/continue` is only for sessions that were already open before.

**New users** (once 0.3.0 is published):
```bash
npm i -g footprint-trace
footprint context install
```

## Not done yet
- **Push:** stuck, see the top.
- **npm publish:** 0.3.0 still needs you to run `! npm login`.
- **OpenCode hook is experimental:** the plugin uses `experimental.chat.system.transform`. OpenCode could change or remove it in an update; if so, `/continue` still works.
- **Notion:** P4 is marked solved there.
