"""footprint switch: replay a Claude Code session as a real OpenCode session.

The full chat (prompts, replies, tool calls + results) is converted to
OpenCode's export format and loaded with `opencode import`, then opened with
`opencode -s <id>` — same conversation, continue typing in OpenCode.
"""
import glob, json, os, random, shutil, string, subprocess, sys, tempfile, time
from datetime import datetime

from . import config, context, transcripts

TOOLS = {"Bash": "bash", "Read": "read", "Edit": "edit", "MultiEdit": "edit", "Write": "write",
         "NotebookEdit": "edit", "Grep": "grep", "Glob": "glob", "WebFetch": "webfetch",
         "WebSearch": "websearch", "TodoWrite": "todowrite", "Task": "task", "Agent": "task"}
KEYS = {"file_path": "filePath", "notebook_path": "filePath", "old_string": "oldString",
        "new_string": "newString", "replace_all": "replaceAll"}
_B62 = string.digits + string.ascii_letters
_seq = [0]


def _id(prefix, ms, descending=False):
    """OpenCode-style id: 12 hex of (ms*4096 + counter) then 14 random base62.
    Sessions use the inverted (descending) form so newest sorts first."""
    _seq[0] += 1
    v = (int(ms) * 0x1000 + _seq[0]) & 0xFFFFFFFFFFFF
    if descending:
        v = ~v & 0xFFFFFFFFFFFF
    return f"{prefix}_{v:012x}" + "".join(random.choices(_B62, k=14))


def _ms(rec, last):
    try:
        ms = datetime.fromisoformat(rec["timestamp"].replace("Z", "+00:00")).timestamp() * 1000
    except (KeyError, ValueError, AttributeError):
        ms = last
    return int(max(ms, last + 1))  # strictly increasing keeps ids and ordering sane


def _project_id(cwd):
    """OpenCode caches the project id in <git-common-dir>/opencode; fall back to root commit, then global."""
    git = lambda *a: subprocess.run(["git", "-C", cwd, *a], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
    common = git("rev-parse", "--path-format=absolute", "--git-common-dir")
    if common and os.path.exists(os.path.join(common, "opencode")):
        return open(os.path.join(common, "opencode"), encoding="utf-8").read().strip()
    root = git("rev-list", "--max-parents=0", "HEAD").splitlines()
    return root[0] if root else "global"


def _model():
    """User's OpenCode default model ("provider/model"), else Big Pickle."""
    try:
        m = json.load(open(os.path.join(config.OPENCODE, "opencode.json"), encoding="utf-8")).get("model")
    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError):
        m = None
    provider, _, model = (m or "opencode/big-pickle").partition("/")
    return provider, model


def convert(path, cwd):
    """Claude Code transcript -> OpenCode export dict ({info, messages})."""
    provider, model = _model()
    first = int(os.path.getmtime(path) * 1000)
    sid = _id("ses", first, descending=True)
    msgs, calls, ms, cur, user_id, title = [], {}, 0, None, None, None

    def part(msg, p):
        p.update(id=_id("prt", ms), sessionID=sid, messageID=msg["info"]["id"])
        msg["parts"].append(p)
        return p

    for line in open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"):
        try:
            rec = json.loads(line)
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            continue
        if rec.get("type") == "ai-title":
            title = rec.get("aiTitle")
        if rec.get("isSidechain") or rec.get("type") not in ("user", "assistant"):
            continue
        ms = _ms(rec, ms or first)
        prompt = context._prompt(rec)
        content = (rec.get("message") or {}).get("content")
        if prompt:
            cur = None
            user_id = _id("msg", ms)
            msg = {"info": {"id": user_id, "sessionID": sid, "role": "user", "time": {"created": ms},
                            "agent": "build", "model": {"providerID": provider, "modelID": model}}, "parts": []}
            part(msg, {"type": "text", "text": prompt})
            msgs.append(msg)
        elif rec.get("type") == "assistant" and isinstance(content, list) and user_id:
            if cur is None:
                cur = {"info": {"id": _id("msg", ms), "sessionID": sid, "role": "assistant", "parentID": user_id,
                                "mode": "build", "agent": "build", "path": {"cwd": cwd, "root": cwd}, "cost": 0,
                                "tokens": {"total": 0, "input": 0, "output": 0, "reasoning": 0,
                                           "cache": {"read": 0, "write": 0}},
                                "modelID": model, "providerID": provider,
                                "time": {"created": ms, "completed": ms}, "finish": "stop"}, "parts": []}
                msgs.append(cur)
            cur["info"]["time"]["completed"] = ms
            for b in content:
                if b.get("type") == "text" and b["text"].strip():
                    part(cur, {"type": "text", "text": b["text"], "time": {"start": ms, "end": ms}})
                elif b.get("type") == "tool_use":
                    inp = {KEYS.get(k, k): v for k, v in (b.get("input") or {}).items()}
                    calls[b.get("id")] = part(cur, {
                        "type": "tool", "tool": TOOLS.get(b["name"], b["name"].lower()), "callID": b.get("id"),
                        "state": {"status": "error", "input": inp, "error": "no result recorded",
                                  "time": {"start": ms, "end": ms}}})
        elif isinstance(content, list):  # tool results come back in user records
            for b in content:
                p = calls.get(b.get("tool_use_id")) if b.get("type") == "tool_result" else None
                if not p:
                    continue
                c = b.get("content")
                out = ("".join(x.get("text", "") for x in c if isinstance(x, dict)) if isinstance(c, list)
                       else str(c or ""))[:config.RESULT_CAP]
                st = p["state"]
                st["time"]["end"] = ms
                if b.get("is_error"):
                    st["error"] = out
                else:
                    st.pop("error", None)
                    st.update(status="completed", output=out, title=str(st["input"].get("command")
                              or st["input"].get("filePath") or st["input"].get("pattern") or p["tool"])[:80],
                              metadata={})
    if not msgs:
        return None
    title = title or msgs[0]["parts"][0]["text"][:60]
    info = {"id": sid, "slug": "from-claude", "projectID": _project_id(cwd), "directory": cwd,
            "title": f"{title} (from Claude Code)", "version": "footprint",
            "time": {"created": first if first < msgs[0]["info"]["time"]["created"] else msgs[0]["info"]["time"]["created"],
                     "updated": ms}}
    return {"info": info, "messages": msgs}


def switch(args=()):
    """`footprint switch [claude-session-id]` — newest Claude session for this dir by default."""
    cwd = os.getcwd()
    pdir = transcripts.project_dir(cwd)
    files = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(pdir, "*.jsonl")), key=os.path.getmtime, reverse=True)
    if args:
        files = [f for f in files if os.path.basename(f).startswith(args[0])]
    path = next((f for f in files if context.state(f)["prompts"]), None)
    if not path:
        sys.exit(f"no Claude Code session found for {cwd}")
    data = convert(path, cwd)
    if not shutil.which("opencode"):
        sys.exit("opencode not found on PATH — install it first: https://opencode.ai")
    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile("w", suffix=".json", delete=False, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump(data, f)
    r = subprocess.run(["opencode", "import", f.name], capture_output=True, text=True)
    os.unlink(f.name)
    if r.returncode:
        sys.exit(f"opencode import failed:\n{r.stderr or r.stdout}")
    sid = data["info"]["id"]
    n = len(data["messages"])
    print(f"imported '{data['info']['title']}' ({n} messages) into OpenCode as {sid}")
    if sys.stdout.isatty():
        os.execvp("opencode", ["opencode", "-s", sid])  # straight into the same chat
    print(f"open it: opencode -s {sid}")


if __name__ == "__main__":  # self-check: tool_use/result pairing + key/tool mapping
    recs = [
        {"type": "ai-title", "aiTitle": "Fix login"},
        {"type": "user", "timestamp": "2026-10-28T10:00:00Z", "message": {"role": "user", "content": "fix login"}},
        {"type": "assistant", "timestamp": "2026-10-28T10:00:01Z", "message": {"role": "assistant", "content": [
            {"type": "text", "text": "looking"},
            {"type": "tool_use", "id": "t1", "name": "Edit", "input": {"file_path": "/a.py", "old_string": "x", "new_string": "y"}},
            {"type": "tool_use", "id": "t2", "name": "Bash", "input": {"command": "pytest"}}]}},
        {"type": "user", "timestamp": "2026-10-28T10:00:02Z", "message": {"role": "user", "content": [
            {"type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": "t1", "content": "ok"},
            {"type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": "t2", "is_error": True, "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "1 failed"}]}]}},
        {"type": "assistant", "timestamp": "2026-10-28T10:00:03Z", "message": {"role": "assistant", "content": [
            {"type": "text", "text": "done"}]}},
        {"type": "user", "timestamp": "2026-10-28T10:00:04Z", "message": {"role": "user", "content": "thanks"}},
    ]
    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile("w", suffix=".jsonl", delete=False, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        fh.write("\n".join(map(json.dumps, recs)))
    d = convert(fh.name, "/tmp/proj")
    os.unlink(fh.name)
    roles = [m["info"]["role"] for m in d["messages"]]
    assert roles == ["user", "assistant", "user"], roles
    a = d["messages"][1]
    edit, bash = [p for p in a["parts"] if p["type"] == "tool"]
    assert edit["tool"] == "edit" and edit["state"]["status"] == "completed"
    assert edit["state"]["input"] == {"filePath": "/a.py", "oldString": "x", "newString": "y"}
    assert bash["state"]["status"] == "error" and bash["state"]["error"] == "1 failed"
    assert [p["text"] for p in a["parts"] if p["type"] == "text"] == ["looking", "done"]
    assert a["info"]["parentID"] == d["messages"][0]["info"]["id"]
    ids = [m["info"]["id"] for m in d["messages"]]
    assert ids == sorted(ids), ids  # ascending ids = chronological order
    assert d["info"]["title"] == "Fix login (from Claude Code)" and d["info"]["id"].startswith("ses_")
    print("switch convert ok")

import glob, json, os, random, shutil, string, subprocess, sys, tempfile, time
from datetime import datetime

from . import config, context, transcripts

TOOLS = {"Bash": "bash", "Read": "read", "Edit": "edit", "MultiEdit": "edit", "Write": "write",
         "NotebookEdit": "edit", "Grep": "grep", "Glob": "glob", "WebFetch": "webfetch",
         "WebSearch": "websearch", "TodoWrite": "todowrite", "Task": "task", "Agent": "task"}
KEYS = {"file_path": "filePath", "notebook_path": "filePath", "old_string": "oldString",
        "new_string": "newString", "replace_all": "replaceAll"}
_B62 = string.digits + string.ascii_letters
_seq = [0]


def _id(prefix, ms, descending=False):
    """OpenCode-style id: 12 hex of (ms*4096 + counter) then 14 random base62.
    Sessions use the inverted (descending) form so newest sorts first."""
    _seq[0] += 1
    v = (int(ms) * 0x1000 + _seq[0]) & 0xFFFFFFFFFFFF
    if descending:
        v = ~v & 0xFFFFFFFFFFFF
    return f"{prefix}_{v:012x}" + "".join(random.choices(_B62, k=14))


def _ms(rec, last):
    try:
        ms = datetime.fromisoformat(rec["timestamp"].replace("Z", "+00:00")).timestamp() * 1000
    except (KeyError, ValueError, AttributeError):
        ms = last
    return int(max(ms, last + 1))  # strictly increasing keeps ids and ordering sane


def _project_id(cwd):
    """OpenCode caches the project id in <git-common-dir>/opencode; fall back to root commit, then global."""
    git = lambda *a: subprocess.run(["git", "-C", cwd, *a], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
    common = git("rev-parse", "--path-format=absolute", "--git-common-dir")
    if common and os.path.exists(os.path.join(common, "opencode")):
        return open(os.path.join(common, "opencode"), encoding="utf-8").read().strip()
    root = git("rev-list", "--max-parents=0", "HEAD").splitlines()
    return root[0] if root else "global"


def _model():
    """User's OpenCode default model ("provider/model"), else Big Pickle."""
    try:
        m = json.load(open(os.path.join(config.OPENCODE, "opencode.json"), encoding="utf-8")).get("model")
    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError):
        m = None
    provider, _, model = (m or "opencode/big-pickle").partition("/")
    return provider, model


def convert(path, cwd):
    """Claude Code transcript -> OpenCode export dict ({info, messages})."""
    provider, model = _model()
    first = int(os.path.getmtime(path) * 1000)
    sid = _id("ses", first, descending=True)
    msgs, calls, ms, cur, user_id, title = [], {}, 0, None, None, None

    def part(msg, p):
        p.update(id=_id("prt", ms), sessionID=sid, messageID=msg["info"]["id"])
        msg["parts"].append(p)
        return p

    for line in open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"):
        try:
            rec = json.loads(line)
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            continue
        if rec.get("type") == "ai-title":
            title = rec.get("aiTitle")
        if rec.get("isSidechain") or rec.get("type") not in ("user", "assistant"):
            continue
        ms = _ms(rec, ms or first)
        prompt = context._prompt(rec)
        content = (rec.get("message") or {}).get("content")
        if prompt:
            cur = None
            user_id = _id("msg", ms)
            msg = {"info": {"id": user_id, "sessionID": sid, "role": "user", "time": {"created": ms},
                            "agent": "build", "model": {"providerID": provider, "modelID": model}}, "parts": []}
            part(msg, {"type": "text", "text": prompt})
            msgs.append(msg)
        elif rec.get("type") == "assistant" and isinstance(content, list) and user_id:
            if cur is None:
                cur = {"info": {"id": _id("msg", ms), "sessionID": sid, "role": "assistant", "parentID": user_id,
                                "mode": "build", "agent": "build", "path": {"cwd": cwd, "root": cwd}, "cost": 0,
                                "tokens": {"total": 0, "input": 0, "output": 0, "reasoning": 0,
                                           "cache": {"read": 0, "write": 0}},
                                "modelID": model, "providerID": provider,
                                "time": {"created": ms, "completed": ms}, "finish": "stop"}, "parts": []}
                msgs.append(cur)
            cur["info"]["time"]["completed"] = ms
            for b in content:
                if b.get("type") == "text" and b["text"].strip():
                    part(cur, {"type": "text", "text": b["text"], "time": {"start": ms, "end": ms}})
                elif b.get("type") == "tool_use":
                    inp = {KEYS.get(k, k): v for k, v in (b.get("input") or {}).items()}
                    calls[b.get("id")] = part(cur, {
                        "type": "tool", "tool": TOOLS.get(b["name"], b["name"].lower()), "callID": b.get("id"),
                        "state": {"status": "error", "input": inp, "error": "no result recorded",
                                  "time": {"start": ms, "end": ms}}})
        elif isinstance(content, list):  # tool results come back in user records
            for b in content:
                p = calls.get(b.get("tool_use_id")) if b.get("type") == "tool_result" else None
                if not p:
                    continue
                c = b.get("content")
                out = ("".join(x.get("text", "") for x in c if isinstance(x, dict)) if isinstance(c, list)
                       else str(c or ""))[:config.RESULT_CAP]
                st = p["state"]
                st["time"]["end"] = ms
                if b.get("is_error"):
                    st["error"] = out
                else:
                    st.pop("error", None)
                    st.update(status="completed", output=out, title=str(st["input"].get("command")
                              or st["input"].get("filePath") or st["input"].get("pattern") or p["tool"])[:80],
                              metadata={})

        return None
    title = title or msgs[0]["parts"][0]["text"][:60]
    info = {"id": sid, "slug": "from-claude", "projectID": _project_id(cwd), "directory": cwd,
            "title": f"{title} (from Claude Code)", "version": "footprint",
            "time": {"created": first if first < msgs[0]["info"]["time"]["created"] else msgs[0]["info"]["time"]["created"],
                     "updated": ms}}

    """`footprint switch [claude-session-id]` — newest Claude session for this dir by default."""
    cwd = os.getcwd()
    pdir = transcripts.project_dir(cwd)

    if args:
        files = [f for f in files if os.path.basename(f).startswith(args[0])]
    path = next((f for f in files if context.state(f)["prompts"]), None)
    if not path:
        sys.exit(f"no Claude Code session found for {cwd}")
    data = convert(path, cwd)
    if not shutil.which("opencode"):
        sys.exit("opencode not found on PATH — install it first: https://opencode.ai")
    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile("w", suffix=".json", delete=False, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump(data, f)
    r = subprocess.run(["opencode", "import", f.name], capture_output=True, text=True)
    os.unlink(f.name)
    if r.returncode:
        sys.exit(f"opencode import failed:\n{r.stderr or r.stdout}")
    sid = data["info"]["id"]
    n = len(data["messages"])
    print(f"imported '{data['info']['title']}' ({n} messages) into OpenCode as {sid}")
    if sys.stdout.isatty():
        os.execvp("opencode", ["opencode", "-s", sid])  # straight into the same chat
    print(f"open it: opencode -s {sid}")

    recs = [
        {"type": "ai-title", "aiTitle": "Fix login"},
        {"type": "user", "timestamp": "2026-10-28T10:00:00Z", "message": {"role": "user", "content": "fix login"}},
        {"type": "assistant", "timestamp": "2026-10-28T10:00:01Z", "message": {"role": "assistant", "content": [
            {"type": "text", "text": "looking"},
            {"type": "tool_use", "id": "t1", "name": "Edit", "input": {"file_path": "/a.py", "old_string": "x", "new_string": "y"}},
            {"type": "tool_use", "id": "t2", "name": "Bash", "input": {"command": "pytest"}}]}},
        {"type": "user", "timestamp": "2026-10-28T10:00:02Z", "message": {"role": "user", "content": [
            {"type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": "t1", "content": "ok"},
            {"type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": "t2", "is_error": True, "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "1 failed"}]}]}},
        {"type": "assistant", "timestamp": "2026-10-28T10:00:03Z", "message": {"role": "assistant", "content": [
            {"type": "text", "text": "done"}]}},
        {"type": "user", "timestamp": "2026-10-28T10:00:04Z", "message": {"role": "user", "content": "thanks"}},
    ]
    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile("w", suffix=".jsonl", delete=False, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        fh.write("\n".join(map(json.dumps, recs)))
    d = convert(fh.name, "/tmp/proj")
    os.unlink(fh.name)
    roles = [m["info"]["role"] for m in d["messages"]]
    assert roles == ["user", "assistant", "user"], roles
    a = d["messages"][1]
    edit, bash = [p for p in a["parts"] if p["type"] == "tool"]
    assert edit["tool"] == "edit" and edit["state"]["status"] == "completed"
    assert edit["state"]["input"] == {"filePath": "/a.py", "oldString": "x", "newString": "y"}
    assert bash["state"]["status"] == "error" and bash["state"]["error"] == "1 failed"
    assert [p["text"] for p in a["parts"] if p["type"] == "text"] == ["looking", "done"]
    assert a["info"]["parentID"] == d["messages"][0]["info"]["id"]
    ids = [m["info"]["id"] for m in d["messages"]]
    assert ids == sorted(ids), ids  # ascending ids = chronological order
    assert d["info"]["title"] == "Fix login (from Claude Code)" and d["info"]["id"].startswith("ses_")
    print("switch convert ok")

content.text:
Yes, it's built: run `footprint switch` and the full Claude chat opens in OpenCode, with every message, reply and tool call, not just the summary. It's committed (`7b31151`); the push is still running in the background.

## Try it
```bash
cd ~/Developer/footprint
python3 footprint.py switch
```
It imports your latest Claude Code chat for this project into OpenCode and opens it straight away. You see the same conversation and keep typing.

This chat is already imported, so you can open it now:
```bash
opencode -s ses_e79185804ffe7LykcZDya8JaG3
```

## How it works
1. footprint reads this project's latest Claude Code session log. Pass a session ID to pick a different one.
2. It converts the session into OpenCode's own export format:
   - your messages and Claude's replies
   - tool calls and their results, with names and arguments renamed to OpenCode's (`Edit` → `edit`, `file_path` → `filePath`)
   - failed tool calls stay marked as errors, and long tool output is cut to 1500 characters
3. `opencode import` loads it as a real OpenCode session, listed under this project.
4. `opencode -s <id>` opens it.

## Tested
- **Imported this session:** 45 messages, 71 completed tool calls and 3 errors. It was filed under the right project.
- **Big Pickle used the full history:** I continued the imported chat and asked for my 3rd message. It answered "what are other eval ?", which isn't in the summary, and also said the npm version is 0.3.0.
- **Not checked:** I could only test with `opencode run`, not how the chat looks in OpenCode's interactive screen. Open it once and tell me if anything looks off.

## Which one to use
| | `switch` | automatic summary |
|---|---|---|
| Shows | the exact full chat | about 1k tokens of summary |
| Cost per turn | high, since the whole history is sent each turn | low |
| Best for | continuing the same task in detail | starting a new task with context |

Long chats can go over the model's context limit. When that happens, OpenCode shortens the history itself (it calls this compaction).

## Limits
- **One direction:** Claude → OpenCode only. Opening an OpenCode chat back in Claude isn't built.
- **Duplicates:** running `switch` again on the same session makes a second copy.

content.text:
A new user needs four steps. Before that, **publish 0.3.0**: npm still has 0.2.0, which installs the old model-first version.

## What they need first
- **Claude Code**, used at least once in their project
- **OpenCode:** `curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install | bash`
- **Python 3.9+** (macOS and Linux usually have it already) and **Node 18+** for npm

## Setup (once)
```bash
npm i -g footprint-trace
footprint context install
```
That's all. No model download and no training.

## Daily use
**1. Work in Claude Code as usual.** Every new session, and every `/clear`, starts already knowing where the last session in that project left off.

**2. Switch to OpenCode** (for example when the Claude quota runs out):
```bash
cd my-project
opencode
```
- The first time, pick Big Pickle with `/models`. It's free for now.
- Then just type. The new session already knows what you were doing.

**3. If you want the exact same chat, not a summary:**
```bash
cd my-project
footprint switch
```
This opens the whole Claude conversation in OpenCode, and you keep typing.

**4. Switch back to Claude any time.** The next Claude session picks up what you did in OpenCode.

## Useful commands
| | |
|---|---|
| `footprint context` | shows what the next session will be given |
| `/continue` in OpenCode | adds the context to a session that was already open |
| `footprint switch <id>` | imports a specific Claude session instead of the latest |

## Things to tell them
- **Same folder:** OpenCode must be opened in the same project folder as the Claude session.
- **Restart OpenCode:** if it was open during `context install`, restart it once.
- **Privacy:** Big Pickle runs on OpenCode's servers, and data may be used to improve the model while it's free. Don't use it on sensitive code.
- **Platforms:** I've only tested on your Mac. Linux should work the same. Windows hasn't been tried.

## Before you share
1. Run `! npm login` and I'll publish 0.3.0.
2. Optionally, test on a clean account or another machine: `npm i -g footprint-trace && footprint context install`, then the steps above.

Want this as a "Getting started" page in Notion, or as the top section of the README? The README already has a shorter Quick start.

content.text:
Not on general benchmarks. On the thing footprint actually does, you can get close and prove it.

**Why not:** benchmarks like SWE-bench measure how strong the model is: reasoning, debugging, long tasks. footprint doesn't change the model; it changes what the model knows when it starts. Big Pickle with perfect context is still Big Pickle. Its scores haven't even been published, so we couldn't compare honestly anyway.

**What footprint does change:** it removes the cost of losing context. Normally a model you switch to starts cold. It re-reads files, asks again, and repeats mistakes that were already fixed. footprint removes that. On continuing an interrupted task, a cheap model with footprint can come close to Claude, especially on routine work.

## A benchmark we can defend: "resume a task"
Take 20–30 real tasks and stop each one halfway through in Claude. Then finish them three ways:

| Setup | Expected |
|---|---|
| A. Claude Opus with the full session | upper limit |
| B. Big Pickle, starting cold | lower limit |
| C. Big Pickle + footprint (summary or `switch`) | **what we sell** |

Measure task success (do the tests pass?), cost in tokens and $, time to the first useful action, and how often it re-asks or repeats work.

The claim then becomes: "footprint gets back X% of Claude's success rate at Y% of the cost." For example, "85% of Opus results at 1/10th the cost". It's honest, backed by numbers, and fits the "X× cheaper" message.

## The route to actually matching Claude's results
That's the router from earlier: the cheap model does routine steps, and hard steps (failing tests, multi-file debugging) go to Opus. You get Opus quality where it matters and a cheap model for everything else. Benchmark C with routing should get close to A.

**My recommendation:**
1. Don't claim "as good as Opus 5.5". Change the Notion positioning to "X% of Claude's results at Y% of the cost".
2. Build the resume-a-task benchmark. That's maybe a day: a task list, a script that runs A, B and C, and a results table.
3. Add the router afterwards, then benchmark again.

Want me to update the claim in Notion and start the benchmark?

content.text:
There was no way to find the ID, so I added `footprint switch list`. Run it inside the project folder:

```bash
cd ~/Developer/PRagent
footprint switch list
```
```
8c349ae5     3.4h ago    1 msgs  ECONNREFUSED on PR connect
673617a2    47.6h ago    8 msgs  PR agent Claude skill

open one: footprint switch <id>   (first 8 chars are enough)
```
Then:
```bash
footprint switch 673617a2
```

- **Short IDs work:** the first 8 characters are enough.
- **Where the topic comes from:** the title Claude Code gave the session, or your first message if it has no title.
- **How many it shows:** the newest 15 sessions for the folder you're in.
- **Without an ID:** `footprint switch` opens the latest session, which is usually what you want.
- **Where IDs live:** Claude Code's `/resume` picker doesn't show them. They're the file names in `~/.claude/projects/<project>/`, and `list` reads them from there.

I tested `list` in footprint and PRagent, and the built-in check still passes. The commit and push are running in the background.

content.text:
Users don't need to wait for npm. They can install the latest version straight from GitHub, which I've tested and added to the README:

```bash
npm i -g https://github.com/Amanlabh/footprint/tarball/main
footprint context install
```

I installed this into a scratch folder: all files were there, and `context` and `switch list` both worked.

## Fixed along the way
- **Banner crash:** installing from GitHub failed because the welcome banner script that runs after install crashed. It's now non-fatal. Pushed.
- **`npm i -g github:Amanlabh/footprint` still doesn't work:** npm links the package to a temporary folder and then deletes it. That's npm's behaviour, not ours, which is why the docs use the tarball link above.

## Getting npm publish back
Your npm log shows a login in progress in the browser right now. That may already be the way through.

1. **Fingerprint / passkey:** if you set up two-factor with a security key or Touch ID, the browser asks for your fingerprint and no code is needed. Run `! npm login --auth-type=web`.
2. **Recovery codes:** npm gave you these when you turned on two-factor (check your password manager or notes). Any one of them replaces the code.
3. **Neither:** contact npm support (npmjs.com/support) to recover the account. It's a check by email and can take days.

Once `npm whoami` prints `amanlabh`, say "publish" and I'll publish 0.3.0.

Never lose your context. ## Positioning > We are solving for context.
Continue your work from where you left off — at X× less than the cost of Claude.
Benchmarks as good as Opus 5.5. - Solving for context: the problem isn't the model, it's losing context every time you switch session, tool, or device. footprint keeps it. - Continue where you left off: start a new session in Claude Code or OpenCode and it already knows the goal, files touched, open todos, and where you stopped. - Fraction of the cost: context carried by footprint + a cheaper model (OpenCode / Big Pickle, local footprint model) instead of re-paying for Claude to rebuild it. - Opus 5.5–level quality: target claim — needs proof before we say it publicly. To make the claims publishable: - [ ] Fill in X: measure cost per resumed task (footprint + cheaper model) vs Claude Opus 5.5 on the same tasks - [ ] Benchmark: run the same task set (e.g. SWE-bench subset + our own resume-a-session tasks) and publish results vs Opus 5.5 - [ ] Only ship "as good as Opus 5.5" in marketing once the numbers back it - [ ] Build the resume-a-task benchmark: 20–30 real tasks interrupted mid-way, finished by (A) Opus with full session, (B) Big Pickle cold, (C) Big Pickle + footprint. Measure success, cost, time-to-first-useful-action, re-asks. - Honest fallback claim if C \< A: "X% of Claude's results at Y% of the cost". Router (cheap model + escalate hard steps to Opus) is the path to true Claude-level results. ## Getting started (for users) Needs: Claude Code (used once in the project), OpenCode (curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install | bash), Python 3.9+, Node 18+. Once: ```bash npm i -g footprint-trace footprint context install ``` Daily: 1. Work in Claude Code as usual — new sessions / /clear already know where you left off. 2. Switch to OpenCode in the same folder (opencode), pick Big Pickle once via /models, just type — it already knows. 3. Want the exact same chat? footprint switch (or footprint switch list → footprint switch <id>). 4. Back to Claude anytime — it picks up OpenCode work too. Notes: same project folder in both tools; restart OpenCode once after install; Big Pickle is hosted + free for a limited time and may use data for training — avoid for sensitive code. ## Release log — GitHub main (Oct 28–29) All pushed to [https://github.com/Amanlabh/footprint](https://github.com/Amanlabh/footprint) — latest 5e4d361. | Commit | What | | --- | --- | | 5e4d361 | docs: install latest straight from GitHub tarball | | 22ff543 | fix: postinstall banner can no longer fail the install (GitHub installs were breaking) | | e4bc151 | footprint switch list — show session ids to pick from | | 7b31151 | footprint switch — open the full Claude chat in OpenCode | | 70e2b05 | Automatic, two-way continuity for OpenCode (plugin + reads OpenCode sessions) | | 11c1c50 | Continuity-first install; local Qwen model is opt-in; v0.3.0 | | 1081a9f | OpenCode /continue command | | aebedc3 | Session continuity via Claude Code SessionStart hook | | 65a118a | footprint eval • epoch-based training length | | 82c029f | Merged PR #7 (community): UTF-8 file I/O regardless of locale | Pending: npm publish of 0.3.0 — blocked on npm 2FA (recover via passkey/browser login, recovery codes, or npm support). Users can install from the GitHub tarball meanwhile. ## Where we are today - footprint = local SLM trained on Claude Code transcripts (~/.claude/projects/*/*.jsonl), MLX LoRA on Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B. - Serves an OpenAI-compatible endpoint (http://127.0.0.1:8399/v1) so Cursor / OpenCode / Codex CLI can use it. - Shipped: GitHub repo Amanlabh/footprint + npm footprint-trace, /footprint skill, marketing site + GitHub-backed personal environment. ## What we ship next ### 1. Real-time conversation continuity — ✅ SHIPPED (v1) Shipped in v1: - footprint context install → Claude Code SessionStart hook: every new session (and after /clear) starts with the previous session's state. - OpenCode /continue [task] command: switch from Claude to OpenCode and pick up where you left off. - State = topic, goal, latest asks, files touched, open todos, last error, where it ended. Capped at \~1k tokens, skipped if older than 7 days, newest session wins. - OpenCode: automatic via plugin + two-way (Claude ↔ OpenCode) — shipped Oct 29. - footprint switch: open the exact same Claude chat in OpenCode — full history (prompts, replies, tool calls + results) imported via opencode import, opened with opencode -s. Tested: Big Pickle quoted earlier messages verbatim. footprint switch list shows session ids to pick from. — shipped Oct 29. - Qwen / local model is now opt-in ("local model mode"): default install has no model download, no training. Use captured context so a new session continues where the previous Claude session left off — live, not after a retrain. - Watch active session transcripts in real time (tail the .jsonl as it grows). - Build a rolling "session state": goal, decisions made, files touched, open TODOs, last error. - On new session start, inject that state as context (skill / MCP resource / system prompt) → zero re-explaining. - Split fast path vs slow path: live context retrieval now, LoRA retrain on a schedule. - Open questions: how much context to inject (token budget), staleness rules, conflict between sessions in the same repo. ### 2. Business & enterprise - Team / org workspaces: shared context across teammates on the same project. - Self-hosted / on-prem deploy — transcripts never leave the company. - SSO (SAML/OIDC), RBAC, audit logs, retention + PII redaction before training. - Admin dashboard: usage, seats, which projects have context. - Per-team adapters (one LoRA per team/repo) with central model registry. - Pricing tiers: Free (local) → Team → Enterprise. ### 3. VS Code wrapper — the dev ecosystem Our own VS Code–based environment, powered by OpenCode + Big Pickle as the agent/model layer. - Users can create & install skills, same model as Claude Code skills (SKILL.md folders). - Users can connect MCP servers, same config shape as Claude (mcpServers JSON) so existing configs just work. - footprint context is built in: every session starts with the project's prior context. - Path: start as a VS Code extension → decide later on full fork (VSCodium-style) if needed. ### 4. Internal Granola-style meeting capture - Built-in meeting notes: record → transcribe → summarize → store as project context. - Meeting decisions flow straight into coding sessions ("we agreed X in standup" is known to the agent). ### 5. On-field voice as context - Capture speech in the field (calls, site visits, walk-and-talk) and turn it into context. - Note: capturing voice → text is STT (speech-to-text); TTS (text-to-speech) would be for reading context/answers back aloud. Likely want both — confirm scope. - Everything lands in the same context store as transcripts + meetings. ## Unified picture Sources (Claude sessions, IDE, meetings, field voice) → footprint context store → delivered to any agent (Claude, OpenCode, our VS Code wrapper) in real time. ## Next steps - [x] Spec the session-state schema for real-time continuity - [x] Context injection: Claude Code SessionStart hook + OpenCode /continue - [x] OpenCode plugin for automatic continuity + read OpenCode sessions back into Claude - [ ] Cost + benchmark numbers vs Opus 5.5 (see Positioning) - [ ] Spike VS Code extension running OpenCode / Big Pickle - [ ] Skills + MCP config compatibility with Claude format - [ ] Pick STT engine (local Whisper / MLX) for meetings + field capture - [ ] Enterprise requirements list (SSO, on-prem, audit, redaction) - [ ] Pricing draft ## What landed

- footprint switch — opens a full Claude Code chat inside OpenCode. Pick a past session and keep working on it in OpenCode instead of Claude. - switch list — lists recent sessions with their ids so you can choose one to resume. - Automatic two-way continuity — new OpenCode sessions start from the newest prior session in the project (Claude Code or OpenCode). No copy-paste. - /continue command — for OpenCode sessions already open, resumes the previous session's state manually.
